task_name: RTE 25% EWS/DG Free-Seat Admission in a Private Unaided School
citizen_input: Parent's online application for an EWS/DG free seat (child's birth proof, income/caste certificate, residence proof, distance declaration)
outcome: Child admitted free of cost to a private unaided school against a reserved 25% seat, reimbursed by the state
source: RTE Act 2009 s.12(1)(c) and s.12(2); Uttarakhand RTE online admission portal (registration, BEO verification, lottery, allotment)

task_name: MGNREGA Job Card Issue and Guaranteed Work Demand
citizen_input: Household application for a job card at the Gram Panchayat, then a dated written application demanding work
outcome: Job card issued and wage employment provided within 15 days (else unemployment allowance), with wages paid within 15 days of work
total_days: ~30 days job-card issue to first wage payment (15 to allot work + 15 to pay wages)
source: MGNREGA 2005 s.3 (15-day work guarantee), s.3(1) unemployment allowance, s.3(3) delayed-wage compensation 0.05%/day; MGNREGA Operational Guidelines 2013 (muster roll, measurement book, GRS/JE roles, wage FTO, social audit)

citizen_input: How do I get a disability (divyang) certificate and UDID card to access benefits?
outcome: A digitally-signed disability certificate (Form V/VI/VII) stating the assessed percentage, and a nationally-valid UDID card downloadable from the portal with a physical PVC card by post; usable to claim RPwD reservations, pension, scholarships, and concessions.
legal_basis: Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, Sections 56-59 (certifying authority, certificate valid across country, appeal); RPwD Rules, 2017, Rule 18 (Forms V/VI/VII/VIII, one-month issuance, ninety-day appeal); Gazette Notification S.O. 76(E) dated 04.01.2018 (assessment guidelines for 21 disabilities); UDID scheme of DEPwD (swavlambancard.gov.in). In UP, delivery is assisted via e-District / Jan Seva Kendra (CSC).
total_days: Approx. 30 days statutory for certificate issuance from receipt (RPwD Rules 2017, Rule 18(3)); physical UDID PVC card typically an additional 30-60 days.

task_name: Land Mutation (Dakhil Kharij / Namantaran) — recording change of ownership in the land record
citizen_input: Application to record a transfer (sale/gift/inheritance) with registered sale-deed / succession documents, filed at the Tehsil
outcome: Khatauni (record of rights) amended to reflect the new owner; certified copy of updated khatauni issued
legal_basis: UP Revenue Code 2006 (ss. 33, 34, 35) / UP Land Records Manual
total_days: ~35-45 days (45-day disposal deadline enforced by state directive; longer if contested)
source: UP Revenue Code 2006, s.35 (mutation; proclamation; uncontested/contested; appeal to SDO within 30 days); UP Revenue Code 2006 ss.33-35 bare act; 45-day dakhil kharij disposal deadline (state directive)

task_name: Building Plan / Housing Construction Permit (Naksha Sanction) in a Nagar Nigam
citizen_input: Building plan drawings (CAD/AutoDCR), site/ownership documents, application fee via the OBPAS single-window portal
outcome: Sanctioned building plan + permit/sanction letter authorizing construction
legal_basis: UP Building Construction & Development Bye-Laws 2008; UP Urban Planning & Development Act 1973; Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011; OBPAS/AutoDCR
total_days: 15-30 days statutory (15 via OBPAS auto-scrutiny; 30 under Building Bye-Laws)
source: UP Building Construction & Development Bye-Laws 2008 (amended 2016); UP OBPAS/AutoDCR single-window portal; Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 (Right to Public Services)

citizen_input: Online application via e-District/CSC (or at Tehsil) with self-declaration, ID, address and supporting proofs
outcome: Digitally-signed caste / income / domicile certificate delivered to the applicant
legal_basis: UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 (Right to Public Services) / e-District UP
total_days: ~7-15 working days (statutory limit under the Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam schedule)
source: UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 (Right to Public Services; first appeal 30 days, second appeal 60 days); e-District UP income/caste/domicile process & Lekhpal verification timelines

task_name: Register a birth and obtain a birth certificate for a newborn
citizen_input: How do I register a birth and get a birth certificate for my newborn?
outcome: A registered birth event and a QR-verified digital birth certificate issued by the Municipal Corporation's Registrar of Births and Deaths via the CRS portal (dc.crsorgi.gov.in), usable as single proof of date of birth.
legal_basis: Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969 (Act 18 of 1969), esp. ss. 8, 10, 12, 13, 17, 23-25, as amended by the Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act, 2023 (Act 20 of 2023, in force 01-Oct-2023, mandating digital registration via the Civil Registration System); delivery timeline and appeals under the Uttar Pradesh Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011 (U.P. Act 3 of 2011) / applicable State Right-to-Public-Services scheme.
total_days: 7 days (statutory registration window: 21 days from birth to report free of charge; certificate delivery within the State Right-to-Service window, commonly 7 working days)

task_name: Register a Death and Obtain a Death Certificate
citizen_input: A family member has died and I need to register the death and get the official death certificate.
outcome: Death registered in the Civil Registration System and an official death certificate issued to the informant/next of kin.
legal_basis: Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969 (ss. 8, 9, 10, 12, 13, 17) as amended by the Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act, 2023 (No. 20 of 2023, in force 1 Oct 2023, mandating CRS-portal registration and digital certificates); state RBD Rules; UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011 / Uttarakhand Right to Service Act (time-bound delivery + appeal ladder).
total_days: Certificate issued free within 7 days of registration completion (RBD Act s.17); registration itself normally same-day when reported within 21 days. Delayed cases add the s.13 permission/order timeline.

task_name: File an FIR / escalate when a police station refuses to register a cognizable-offence complaint (Uttar Pradesh)
citizen_input: Oral or written account of the offence; identity/contact details; for the electronic/e-FIR route a signature furnished within 3 days; for SP/magistrate escalation a copy of the earlier complaint and proof it was submitted (registered-post receipt); for the magistrate application an affidavit and copies of the SHO and SP complaints.
outcome: FIR registered against a free copy issued to the complainant, and investigation of the cognizable offence commenced — either at the station, or after SP direction, or on magistrate order.
legal_basis: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 — s.173(1) (mandatory FIR registration for cognizable offences, free copy, zero-FIR, electronic information), s.173(3) (14-day preliminary enquiry only for 3-7 year offences), s.174 (non-cognizable), s.173(4) (complaint to Superintendent of Police on refusal), s.175(3) (Magistrate's power to direct registration/investigation), s.223 (private complaint on oath); Lalita Kumari v. Govt. of U.P. (2014) 2 SCC 1 (registration mandatory); U.P. Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011 (service-guarantee appeal clocks).
total_days: Registration at the station is same-day / immediate under s.173(1); the SP (s.173(4)) and Magistrate (s.175(3)) routes have no hard statutory day-count in BNSS. Where the grievance is routed as a service default, the U.P. Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam gives a 30-day first-appeal and 60-day second-appeal window.

task_name: Register a sale deed and transfer property ownership (Uttar Pradesh)
citizen_input: How do I register a sale deed and legally transfer ownership when buying property?
outcome: Sale deed registered at the Sub-Registrar's office (conveying ownership) and, subsequently, the revenue record of rights (khatauni) and property-tax records mutated into the buyer's name via dakhil kharij (namantaran).
legal_basis: Registration Act, 1908 (esp. §17 compulsory registration of immovable-property transfers, §23 four-month presentation window, §34 enquiry/appearance of executants, §72 appeal against refusal); Indian Stamp Act, 1899 as applied in UP (stamp duty on market/circle-rate value); Uttar Pradesh Revenue Code, 2006 (§34 registering authority's intimation to Tehsildar and mutation of record of rights; §35 appeal to Sub-Divisional Officer/SDM; §210 revision to Commissioner); Income-tax Act, 1961 §194-IA (1% TDS on consideration ≥ ₹50 lakh); Uttar Pradesh Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011 (time-bound delivery, per-service limits notified under §3, first appeal within 30 days under §6).
total_days: Registration is same-day once the Sub-Registrar appointment is reached (deed returned within days after scanning/indexing); mutation (dakhil kharij) typically 30-45 days for an undisputed case. A registered document must in any case be presented within 4 months of execution (Registration Act §23).
source: https://igrsup.gov.in/; https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/19960/1/english2011.pdf; https://indiankanoon.org/doc/853279/; https://indiankanoon.org/doc/186589914/; https://bor.up.nic.in/pdf/Proposed_Amendment_English.pdf; https://upbhulekh.gov.in/; https://vaad.up.nic.in/; https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/uttar-pradesh-property-registration; https://cleartax.in/s/stamp-duty-and-regi

task_name: New domestic electricity connection for a house
citizen_input: Applicant's address and sanctioned load required (kW); ID proof (Aadhaar/Voter ID/Passport/PAN); proof of ownership/occupancy of premises (registered sale deed / partition / succession / heir certificate, or rent agreement + owner NOC); recent photograph; mobile number and email; APL/BPL category.
outcome: A metered, energized domestic electricity connection released by the area DISCOM (in UP: a UPPCL DISCOM such as PVVNL/MVVNL/PuVVNL/DVVNL; in Uttarakhand: UPCL) at the sanctioned load, after payment of the demand-note charges and security deposit.
legal_basis: Electricity Act, 2003 (s.43 universal duty to supply); Electricity (Rights of Consumers) Rules, 2020 (as amended); UP Electricity Supply Code, 2005 (UPERC) governing application, demand note and release timelines (cl. 4.15/4.16) — in Uttarakhand, UERC Electricity Supply Code; UPERC (Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum & Electricity Ombudsman) Regulations, 2022 for appeals. Delivered via the Jhatpat Connection Scheme portal (upenergy.in).
total_days: ~7 days (domestic, no line extension) to ~15-30 days; Jhatpat scheme targets ~10 days

task_name: Ration Card (New / Member Addition) under NFSA
citizen_input: Application form + Aadhaar, residence/income proof, family details via e-district/CSC/Supply Office
outcome: Ration card issued (priority/AAY category) with a Fair Price Shop assigned
legal_basis: National Food Security Act 2013 (ss. 10, 12, 14, 16); state TPDS Control Order; e-district
total_days: 30 days statutory (NFSA inspection/verification norm); card collectable up to ~45 days in practice
source: National Food Security Act 2013 (ss.10,12,14,16); Uttarakhand FCS Dept URCMS / e-PDS ration-card process; NFSA 30-day inspection/verification norm; DGRO -> State Food Commission appeal

task_name: Apply for the Old-Age (Vridha) Pension for a senior citizen with no regular income
citizen_input: How do I apply for the old-age (vridha) pension as a senior citizen with no regular income?
outcome: A monthly old-age pension (UP SSPY: currently ~Rs 1,000/month; Uttarakhand: Rs 1,500/month) is sanctioned by the District Social Welfare Officer / District Probation Officer and credited quarterly to the applicant's Aadhaar-linked bank account by DBT/NEFT.
legal_basis: Delivered as the state Social Security / Vridhavastha Pension (Samajik Suraksha Pension Yojana, SSPY, in UP) layered on the central Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS) under the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP); time-bound-delivery and appeal backstopped by the Uttar Pradesh Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011 (UP Act 3 of 2011) / Uttarakhand Right to Service Act. Administered by the state Department of Social Welfare / Directorate of Social Welfare via the Integrated Pension Portal (sspy-up.gov.in / ssp.uk.gov.in).
total_days: Approx. 30-60 days from complete application to sanction; pension then paid quarterly via NEFT/DBT.

task_name: Widow / Destitute Woman (Nirashrit Mahila) Pension after husband's death
citizen_input: How do I get a widow (nirashrit mahila) pension after my husband's death?
outcome: Applicant's name is added to the widow-pension roll and ₹1,000/month (₹500 state + ₹500 central) is disbursed quarterly (₹3,000) by DBT into her Aadhaar-linked bank account.
legal_basis: UP Nirashrit Mahila (Widow) Pension Scheme administered by the Women Welfare Department (Mahila Kalyan Vibhag) via the Integrated Social Pension Portal (sspy-up.gov.in); registration of husband's death under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969; income/domicile certificates and service time-limits under the U.P. Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011 (Right to Public Services); disbursement via DBT/PFMS.
total_days: Approx. 90-120 days end-to-end once prerequisite certificates are in hand (verification 45 days + block review 15 days + district-committee sanction ~30 days + PFMS/DBT ~30 days); prerequisite certificates add 7-30 days.
